title: AD, AS and the Multiplier
welcome_lead: Aggregate demand, aggregate supply and the multiplier explain output.

final_note: Output equilibrium sits where AD meets AS - shocks shift both.

walkthroughs.body_html: The AD curve shows total spending at each price level. Components are Consumption, Investment, Government spending and net X minus M exports.
SRAS slopes up because wages and contracts adjust slowly. LRAS is vertical at full employment - long run, only supply-side reforms shift it.
An extra 100 pounds of government spending becomes income for the receiver, who spends MPC of it, and so on. With MPC = 0.5, the multiplier is 1 / 0.5 = 2.

mcqs.q: What components make up aggregate demand?
options: AD = C + I + G + (X - M): consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. A shift in any component shifts the AD curve.
Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
The multiplier is the rate at which interest compounds.
Aggregate demand is just the total amount consumers want to buy.

mcqs.q: What determines the size of the fiscal multiplier?
options: The fiscal multiplier is the rate of growth of the money supply.
Mainly the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) — the higher the share of extra income people spend domestically, the bigger the multiplier. Leakages (saving, imports, taxes) reduce the multiplier.
The multiplier is the rate at which interest compounds.
The fiscal multiplier is always 2 or 3.
